newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: Zambian court adjourns electoral rigging case.
newsitem.headline: Zambian court adjourns electoral rigging case.

text.p: Zambia's supreme court on Wednesday postponed a hearing in which four opposition political parties are challenging the outcome of last year's general election won by President Frederick Chiluba.
The court adjourned the case indefinitely after lawyers for the four parties requested time to review their case.
Lawyer Patrick Mvunga said their case had been weakened by Tuesday's court decision to dismiss the petition against the electoral commission which they are accusing of helping to rig the election.
The court however ruled that the petition against Chiluba and his Movement for Multiparty Democracy (MMD) may proceed.
"It will be extremely difficult for us to pursue the case that the elections were rigged if we cannot adduce evidence from the electoral commission," Mvunga told the court.
"The courts ruling has left us feeling like a passenger plane without radar," he added.
The parties are claiming that the commission conspired with the MMD to rig the elections by, among other things, tampering with the voters register.
They also claim that Chiluba lied about his nationality and parentage in filing his electoral nomination papers.
